A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Chroma forecasting study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including the renumbered detailed benchmark tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting experiments on Chronos Benchmark II and GIFT-Eval, portfolio ablations, scaling analyses, and synthetic-data bias–variance measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a numerical breakdown of the scratch-trained versus post-trained portfolio comparison.

M1.justification: The Chronos-Bolt architecture, specialist construction through post-training, quantile-loss objective, model selection, and greedy ensembling remain unchanged. Added explanations do not introduce a different procedure.

E1.justification: The training corpus and domain/frequency partitions, BM2 and GIFT-Eval coverage, and synthetic bias–variance task are retained. The new appendix table uses existing BM2 coverage.

E2.justification: Benchmark comparator membership is unchanged. Scratch-trained portfolios were already compared with post-trained portfolios in v1's ablations; v2 Table 9 expands their reporting. Newly cited Time-MoE and Moirai-MoE are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Model sizes, training budgets, metrics, aggregation, and held-out validation procedure remain unchanged. Section 4 clarifies rolling-window selection and subsequent reuse; using multiple selection windows is described as a possibility, not a newly conducted evaluation.

E4.justification: New Appendix G.4.1 and Table 9 expand the existing scratch-versus-post-training ablation with WQL and MASE broken down jointly by model size, partition type, and combination strategy. This provides additional quantitative detail for an existing question rather than introducing a new ablation.

E5.justification: Reported repetition counts, scaling-significance conventions, and mixed-linear-model ablation testing remain unchanged. Tables 6 and 8 contain revised p-values, but v2 does not document a different statistical or uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Table 9 adds scratch-trained result entries, including 4m frequency-ensemble WQL 0.893 and MASE 0.882. Existing p-values also change: Table 6's frequency MASE value changes from 0.046 to 0.0536, and Table 8's domain WQL value from 0.015 to 0.08575, crossing 0.05. Headline benchmark scores and the six matched detailed benchmark tables remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The ensemble-weighting formulation, FLOP calculations, and bias–variance definitions and reasoning in Appendices D–F are retained. The added main-text bias explanation summarizes reasoning already present in v1's appendix.

C1.justification: The central claims about competitive small-model portfolios, efficient specialist post-training, and test-time selection or ensembling remain unchanged. The introduction now names the already-used encoder-decoder Chronos-Bolt architecture without introducing a different contribution.

C2.justification: The limitations now explicitly acknowledge that experiments cover encoder-decoder transformers and leave other architectures untested. Appendix G.4.1 additionally qualifies the scratch-versus-post-training comparison by stating that individual-task results yield no clear general conclusion.

D1.justification: Architectural hyperparameters, optimization settings, hardware, training times, dataset references, and ensemble-selection implementation details are retained. The expanded validation discussion clarifies the existing procedure rather than supplying a new implementation setting or resource.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 and the references add Time-MoE and Moirai-MoE, connecting the existing mixture-of-experts discussion specifically to time-series forecasting. The broader positioning around independently trained specialists and flexible test-time combination remains intact.

P1.justification: Localized additions explain validation and existing bias–variance reasoning, revise limitations, and introduce Appendices G.4.1 and H, the latter disclosing limited editorial LLM use. Affiliations and publication headers also change, while the overall narrative structure is preserved.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 9, combining retained portfolio rows with scratch-trained rows. Table 2 moves from page 8 to page 9, some figures and text shift, and Figure 1's caption formatting changes. Existing graphical content and detailed benchmark table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Table 9 makes the existing training-strategy comparison easier to assess, while clearer validation explanations, explicit architectural limitations, and relevant MoE citations improve precision and context. These are limited gains to an otherwise stable study. The unexplained p-value revisions in Tables 6 and 8 do not establish improved statistical rigor.
